targets.approach: From Valdez drive up Thompson Pass and leave the car at the large pullout beside Odyssey Lake, level with the 27-mile post. Cross the road to the streambed and follow it up until the crag appears on the left. The line climbs a crack set in a corner, clips a bolt, pulls a small roof, and ends up the short face over it.
targets.name: 27 Mile

targets.approach: The Mendenhall Towers stand north of Juneau and can be reached by helicopter from town; the other ways are to ski north along Blackerby Ridge toward the glacier's northern fork, or to climb the glacier itself from the West Glacier trail. The glacier below The Curtain has the largest flat stretch beneath the towers and serves as the landing and camp spot for south-side routes, which need basic glacier travel skills. Looking from the Fourth Tower's south side, find the broad couloir descending; the buttress forming its left edge holds The Mammoth, on a crack system running from the glacier up to the right of a feature shaped like a mammoth's trunk.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the bolted rappel line down the route, keeping the ropes out of the cracks in the upper part.
targets.name: The Mammoth

targets.approach: The 5390 massif sits in the middle of Baranof Island east of Sitka and is remote. One approach begins where the gate blocks Sawmill Creek Road, and continues by bike or on foot to an old gravel pit beyond the hatchery, then follows flagging to the southern flank of Cross Mountain and links a chain of ridges to the massif; allow a full day. A shorter approach rides the road to Green Lake, crosses the lake by kayak, and climbs flagged ground to the ridge and across the alpine. Parties camp on the level snow shelf beneath the west face, and the routes are spread along the foot of that face from camp. All That for a Hand Crack? is on the southernmost formation of the west face, to the right of Fossilized Potential. It starts up a diagonal, left-leaning double crack.
targets.name: All That for a Hand Crack?

targets.approach: The 5390 massif sits in the middle of Baranof Island east of Sitka and is remote. One approach begins where the gate blocks Sawmill Creek Road, and continues by bike or on foot to an old gravel pit beyond the hatchery, then follows flagging to the southern flank of Cross Mountain and links a chain of ridges to the massif; allow a full day. A shorter approach rides the road to Green Lake, crosses the lake by kayak, and climbs flagged ground to the ridge and across the alpine. Parties camp on the level snow shelf beneath the west face, and the routes are spread along the foot of that face from camp. Granitic Dreams is the prominent dihedral along the left edge of its formation, entered from a slightly loose corner below the main dihedral.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the south over the snow, the same way as the other west face routes. Rappelling the route is not advised, because it is long.
targets.name: Granitic Dreams

targets.approach: Angstroms is a large crag of soft, crumbly rock, found by driving north on the Kougarok road a little beyond Bear Mountain. Goshawk is on the left side of the crag, following a flake on the south face.
targets.name: Goshawk

targets.approach: From Haines head out the highway and park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch, follow the creek past the culvert, and take the flagged trail up into the woods to a boulder field. For Bear Spray Wall cross the boulder field angling up and right, then follow the flagged trail past three small chossy cliffs to the wall. The route starts at the first obvious trad line on arriving at the wall, as for Spray Some on Yourself, going up a ramp to the left and out of an alcove, then follows a crack to the right.
targets.name: Spray some on your friends

targets.approach: From Haines head out the highway and park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch, follow the creek past the culvert, and take the flagged trail up into the woods to a boulder field. For Bear Spray Wall cross the boulder field angling up and right, then follow the flagged trail past three small chossy cliffs to the wall. It is the first trad line that heads directly upward when you arrive at the wall: a short ramp up and left leads to an alcove, then the line goes straight up into the hand crack.
targets.name: Spray some on yourself

targets.approach: Drive into Red Rock Canyon about halfway, to the bend where the big pile of red debris nears the road, and park in any of the pullouts after it. Look east for the prominent ridge that reaches the canyon floor with little brush, and hike it to the rim. Cross the tundra plateau from the west rim to the east rim; the alpine lake below Canwell Peak comes into view, and the crag sits just south, nearer the peak, at the top of the plateau. 3 Bears is the left crack on the last vertical wall, downhill and to the right.
targets.name: 3 Bears

targets.approach: Drive into Red Rock Canyon about halfway, to the bend where the big pile of red debris nears the road, and park in any of the pullouts after it. Look east for the prominent ridge that reaches the canyon floor with little brush, and hike it to the rim. Cross the tundra plateau from the west rim to the east rim; the alpine lake below Canwell Peak comes into view, and the crag sits just south, nearer the peak, at the top of the plateau. Pilot Car is at the far left of the crag, and is the first line seen when you walk down the access gully on the south side to the base.
targets.name: Pilot Car

targets.approach: Drive into Red Rock Canyon about halfway, to the bend where the big pile of red debris nears the road, and park in any of the pullouts after it. Look east for the prominent ridge that reaches the canyon floor with little brush, and hike it to the rim. Cross the tundra plateau from the west rim to the east rim; the alpine lake below Canwell Peak comes into view, and the crag sits just south, nearer the peak, at the top of the plateau. Power Outage lies toward the right-hand end of the crag, inside the main amphitheater.
targets.name: Power Outage

targets.approach: Drive into Red Rock Canyon about halfway, to the bend where the big pile of red debris nears the road, and park in any of the pullouts after it. Look east for the prominent ridge that reaches the canyon floor with little brush, and hike it to the rim. Cross the tundra plateau from the west rim to the east rim; the alpine lake below Canwell Peak comes into view, and the crag sits just south, nearer the peak, at the top of the plateau. Richardson Washout follows an acute dihedral right around the corner from Pilot Car.
targets.name: Richardson Washout

targets.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. Chicken Rock is a smaller rock that resembles a chicken, set above and to the right of the Southeast Buttress and below and to the right of the East Tower. Corner is the large corner system high on the formation's left side, as seen walking up to the rock.
targets.name: Corner

targets.approach: Little Switzerland on the Pika Glacier is reached by air taxi from Talkeetna. From the landing strip, ski or snowshoe up the glacier to Crown Jewel, the wide formation beside the Munchkin and the Royal Tower. The route begins from the saddle between Crown Jewel and the Royal Tower, between the Pika and Crown glaciers, on the Crown Jewel flank, at a buttress with a large hanging glacier on its west side. Cross the bergschrund and angle up and right on steepening snow to the rock below a big right-facing corner.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route rather than downclimbing the snow and crossing the bergschrund again.
targets.name: Crown Royal

targets.approach: Devil's Thumb is reached by helicopter from Petersburg or by boat and foot from the coast. This route is on the south side. The approach comes up from the Cauldron beneath it, following a ramp system in the rock beside the southern icefall's west edge, a spot that suits a helicopter drop. A second way is to descend from the upper base camp, which passes under some objective hazard. Either way, cross the upper pocket glacier to the lower-angle rock ridge that leads to the south pillar, mostly third and fourth class with a little fifth. The first pitch begins from the notch under the south pillar.
targets.descent_text: Descend the route by rappel, using the face below the traverse until you re-enter the large corner system.
targets.name: South Pillar - Free

targets.approach: Park at Black Rapids Lodge, or at the Richardson Highway pullout at mile 227, and take the trail from the lodge to the pipeline cut. Walk south along the cut to Gunnysack Creek and continue into the canyon. The line is on one of the few outcrops along Gunnysack's south ridge; search for an arete that drops the whole way from the canyon rim.
targets.descent_text: Walk off by bushwhacking across to the neighbouring hill, then take the trails back down to Gunnysack.
targets.name: Stairway to Heaven

targets.approach: Lion's Head is a big igneous intrusion overlooking the Matanuska Glacier, reached from a pullout off the Glenn Highway near the communications tower. From the pullout take the trail, and cut right where it steepens. Sidehill around to the talus and descend along the cliff edge. The route climbs the west-facing cliff above Coyote Creek and starts below a clean face, taking the left line of the two weaknesses.
targets.name: Shit in the Eye

targets.approach: From Palmer take North Palmer Fishhook Road to the Mother Lode Lodge switchback, then Archangel Road past the bridge to the Reed Lakes trailhead. The trail winds up to an abandoned cabin, where the climbing in the basin begins. Mile High Wall is approached by climbing the drainage that comes down from the west to the trail connecting the two lakes. Main Wall is at the centre of the cliff, right of the Shield and below the Diving Board. Air Sex Society starts on the slab below the dihedral.
targets.name: Air Sex Society

targets.approach: From Palmer take North Palmer Fishhook Road to the Mother Lode Lodge switchback, then Archangel Road past the bridge to the Reed Lakes trailhead. The trail winds up to an abandoned cabin, where the climbing in the basin begins. Mile High Wall is approached by climbing the drainage that comes down from the west to the trail connecting the two lakes. Main Wall is at the centre of the cliff, right of the Shield and below the Diving Board. Moon Pilot begins in a short, low-angle, left-facing dihedral leading to a small ledge.
targets.descent_text: Walk off, or rappel over the large roof from the separate two-bolt anchor that belongs to a different route.
targets.name: Moon Pilot

targets.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. Birthday on the Sheep Trail takes the big weakness in the middle of the Main Wall, to the left of the Keyhole and the bear cave; hiking on around the slabby apron means you have overshot it. It starts just right of the loose rock that forms the obvious weakness.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right, down toward the East Tower and back to camp.
targets.name: Birthday on the Sheep Trail

targets.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. Godiva is a variation on the finish of Ghirardelli: as you come to the top of its grass gully, head right of the tower to a single-bolt anchor, which is the start. The line follows a distinct ledge, with the wall dropping off to its right.
targets.name: Godiva

targets.approach: The wall stands at the north end of the New Harbor at Valdez. Leave the vehicle just to the south of it, out of the way of fishing activity. Harbor Fever is among the first vertical cracks you meet counting from the wall's right end.
targets.descent_text: Rappel off the alders, or walk off along the main trail.
targets.name: Harbor Fever

targets.approach: The Trolls are summits just south of the Throne in Little Switzerland, in Denali National Park, reached by air taxi from Talkeetna. Approach North Troll via the glacier from the landing strip. The route follows the northeast ridge and then the north face.
targets.name: Northeast Ridge

targets.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. The Razorback is a small cragging spot between the Southeast Buttress and the East Tower: hike up and right of the buttress to just below the tower, with the lines on the formation's right-hand side as seen when walking up. Razorbutt is a wide crack on the formation's rear face; climb the slope and curl behind the rock to find it.
targets.name: Razorbutt

targets.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. The Southeast Buttress is the feature on the right side of the main wall. Hike up and swing right round the buttress, past the small formation called Razorback; the first pitch begins just above it.
targets.descent_text: After the last pitch, untie, walk to the true summit, and descend to the right into the amphitheatre; it returns you to the base of the climb.
targets.name: Barnyard Betty

targets.approach: From Palmer, take North Palmer Fishhook Road to the Mother Lode Lodge switchback, then the gravel Archangel Road, and follow it past the bridge to the Reed Lakes trailhead. The trail winds up to an abandoned cabin, where the climbing and bouldering in the basin begins. Spirit Boulder Area lies left of the approach gully that serves Shield, Main Wall and Two Toke Tower, and Cali Slit is left of the Spirit Boulder chalice. It slabs past two bolts into a roof, then crosses the lip into a left-trending slit.
targets.name: Cali Slit

targets.approach: Little Switzerland on the Pika Glacier in Denali National Park is reached by air taxi from Talkeetna, and the approach from Pika base camp to The Throne is very short. The route climbs the formation's west face, just left of a roof coated in vivid green lichen, starting off snow onto an easy unprotected face leading to a moderate crack system and a large ledge, before merging into the northwest ridge near the formation's midpoint. It begins left of Swisser than Swiss Chocolate and right of the popular single-pitch cragging cracks.
targets.descent_text: From the west summit, go down The Lost Marsupial route on the formation's south side to reach the glacier.
targets.name: Oxidado Express

targets.approach: Heading out from Haines, park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch and follow the creek past the culvert to a flagged trail into the woods, which leads to a boulder field. A trail runs up the right side of the boulder field to the main wall, arriving at the base of Chest Fur, with the routes lying to its right. Dancing in Your XtraTufs is the farthest-right route on the Weird Alaska wall; it begins by clipping a bolt and moving left on exposed ground to a ledge.
targets.name: Dancing in your XtraTufs

targets.approach: Heading out from Haines, park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch and follow the creek past the culvert to a flagged trail into the woods, which leads to a boulder field. A trail runs up the right side of the boulder field to the main wall, arriving at the base of Chest Fur, with the routes lying to its right. Unnamed 4 is the obvious overhanging crack as you move right along the wall.
targets.name: Unnamed 4
